artifacts.synopsis: The SJC remanded the case to Central Indiana Presbytery with instructions to appoint a committee to reinvestigate under BCO 31-2, after its non-judicial commission declined to find a strong presumption of guilt against an accused teaching elder. The dissent argued the SJC failed to give proper great deference under BCO 39-3.3 to the presbytery's investigative commission's discretionary judgment declining to indict, and that the BCO does not require the investigative procedures ordered by the Decision.

artifacts.title: Jones v. Louisiana
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Jones et al. against Louisiana Presbytery, finding that LAP erred in two ways: first, in failing to apply the correct constitutional standard for determining whether TE Wilkins had differences with the Westminster Standards (differences need not involve overt contradiction or denial, but can arise from different interpretations of wording or biblical exegesis); and second, in failing to adequately investigate and evaluate such differences as required by RAO 16-3(e)(5), thereby neglecting its duty to condemn erroneous opinions that injure the peace or purity of the church.
